claims.text: The alloy is a single-crystal, equiatomic FeNiCrMn high-entropy alloy.
The stated material is the five-component CoCrFeMnNi Cantor alloy.
The initial crystal structure is FCC.
The as-annealed initial state is precipitate-free and has minimal defects.
Yield-strength insensitivity to strain rate is driven predominantly by thermally activated dislocation glide over chemical short-range-order obstacles.
Dislocation nucleation is not the dominant process controlling yield onset.
FCC-to-BCC phase transformation is not the primary deformation mode.
Chemical short-range-order clusters and local lattice distortions produce a heterogeneous energy landscape for dislocation glide.
High lattice friction and local chemical fluctuations create a distributed energy landscape in which thermal activation assists dislocation motion.
The distributed nature of the obstacles produces a large activation volume.
Thermally activated glide with a large activation volume leads to weak strain-rate sensitivity.
The tensile axis should be oriented to maximize resolved shear stress on FCC {111}<110> slip systems.
The crystal orientation should minimize the activation volume for dislocation glide.
Yield strength will vary minimally over strain rates from 10^-4 to 10^2 s^-1.
Yield strength will decrease slightly with increasing temperature because thermal activation is enhanced.
No BCC phase will be detected during deformation.
Observed dislocation structures will indicate glide rather than nucleation-dominated deformation.
Pure Ni and Cu exhibit strong strain-rate sensitivity caused by dislocation nucleation and pile-up mechanisms.
Below 400 K, BCC transformation is thermodynamically unfavorable in this alloy.
If FCC-to-BCC transformation controls yielding, BCC diffraction peaks should appear at yield onset and yield strength should have strong strain-rate dependence.

contradictions.description: The material is alternately identified as four-component FeNiCrMn and as five-component CoCrFeMnNi (the Cantor alloy), so the alloy system and meaning of 'equiatomic' are internally inconsistent.
The orientation constraint calls for minimizing activation volume, whereas the proposed mechanism attributes weak rate sensitivity to a large activation volume.
